questions: Does the oval finish rate stay near 95 percent with this span, confirming that the iteration 9 result is repeatable?
Does the s-bend or slalom line loss stay at 1 per run with max_error at the 0.06 m floor? If so, the remaining gain is controller-side only.
Is the final-track score sensitive to span? A ±0.04 m bar is the best measured, so any further span change should be treated as untested.

intent: Final-iteration handover. Restore the iteration 9 geometry, which is the best-measured platform, and reject the wider ±0.06 m span that cut the oval finish rate from 95 percent to 25 percent. The Integrator should build the controller on this body and sensor bar. Only sensor span and pitch change from iteration 10; all other fields match iteration 9.
learning: Across 11 iterations, the wider ±0.06 m span (iteration 10) cut the oval finish rate sharply and raised steering oscillation, while the single line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom did not clear. The lesson is that the span should stay at ±0.04 m with the 16 mm footprint at y = 0.04 m. All other geometry levers (pitch, footprint, track, mass, wheel radius, lead) were flat, so the controller is the remaining source of gain.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the job is to hand the Integrator the geometry with the strongest race evidence. Iteration 9 (the best raced design, 363.7) ran on the 0.016 m footprint, 20 mm pitch at x = -0.04 to +0.04, y = 0.04 m, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m and mass 0.4 kg. Its oval finished 19 of 20 runs, and max_error on the oval fell to 0.037 m. Iteration 10 widened the span to x = ±0.06 m (30 mm pitch) and scored 209.7. The oval finish rate dropped to 25 percent and steering_oscillation rose to 0.32, while the s-bend line losses fell only from 1.0 to 0.1 and still ended off_track. So the wider span is a net loss on the tracks that matter most for the score. Every earlier geometry test (pitch, footprint, track, mass, wheel radius and lead) left max_error at the floor, so none of them offers a proven gain. I therefore revert the geometry to the iteration 9 platform. Its span of ±0.04 m is the only one with a measured oval finish rate near 95 percent. An untested intermediate span (for example ±0.05 m) would be a gamble on the final unseen track, so I do not propose it. Expected result: a score near the iteration 9 level on the development tracks, with the oval finishing reliably and the s-bend and slalom still limited by the single line loss per run.
